blocks.content: You've been told the application is slow in some regions but not others. Before you explore your services, make sure you have a Pyroscope data source, then open Profiles Drilldown and focus on the signal that matters.

This journey uses a Pyroscope data source named `grafanacloud-play-profiles` that points at the public play instance. The next step checks whether you already have it and helps you add it if you don't.

blocks.description: Create the grafanacloud-play-profiles Pyroscope data source when it is missing.

whenTrue.content: You already have the **grafanacloud-play-profiles** data source. You'll select it in the next step.

whenFalseSectionConfig.title: Add the play Profiles data source

whenFalse.content: You don't have the **grafanacloud-play-profiles** data source yet. Create it with the following steps.
Open **Connections > Data sources > Add new data source**.
Select **Grafana Pyroscope** from the list of data source types.

whenFalse.reftarget: [data-testid='data-testid Data source settings page name input field']
whenFalse.content: At the top of the page, rename the data source to `grafanacloud-play-profiles`.
Click **Save & test**. You should see a message confirming the data source is working.

blocks.content:
With the data source in place, open Profiles Drilldown and choose it.

To explore your services, complete the following steps:
On the Grafana Cloud home page, open the navigation menu and click **Drilldown > Profiles**.

Select **grafanacloud-play-profiles** as the **Data source**.

The **All services** view shows a chart for each service. You can filter by service name to narrow the list.

Make sure the **CPU** profile type (`process_cpu`) is selected.

CPU time helps you identify bottlenecks where operations take too long. You'll see that services use different languages (Go, Java), and some take longer than others, with periodic large spikes.
Optional detour: before you drill in, take a quick look at every profile type `checkoutservice` emits.

The **Profile types** tab shows every signal `checkoutservice` emits at once: CPU (`process_cpu`), memory (`alloc_space`, `inuse_space`), `goroutine` count, and mutex/block `contentions` and `delay`. Each panel has its own **Labels** and **Flame graph** shortcut. Scanning these confirms CPU is the profile type with the telling periodic spikes, the signal worth chasing here.
Return to the **All services** view to continue.
With a profile type chosen, you'll drill into `checkoutservice` next.
